cards.text: The chapter before ends with a shout: "See, your Savior comes!" (Isaiah 62:11). Now Someone appears, marching in from Edom, the people descended from Esau (Genesis 36:1), coming from Bozrah. He's robed in splendor, marching in the greatness of His strength.

cards.question: The One marching in from Edom has stained garments. What color is the stain?

cards.text: Then comes the question everybody's thinking: Who is this? Nobody has to introduce Him. He answers for Himself: "It is I, proclaiming vindication."

cards.question: Proclaiming vindication, the One from Edom says He is mighty to do what?
Next comes the question of why His clothes are red. They look like the garments of someone who does what?

cards.text: He answers, "I have trodden the winepress," the place where grapes got stomped underfoot. Me? I've never stomped ANYTHING, friend, because I don't have feet, I have a gold base and a whole lot of confidence.

cards.question: He says He trod the winepress ___, and no one from the nations was with Him.

cards.text: Then the picture turns, and it isn't grapes anymore. He says, "I trampled them in My anger and trod them down in My fury."

cards.question: As He tramples them down in His fury, what spatters His garments?

cards.text: So why all this? He tells us exactly what was in His heart.

cards.question: He says the day of ___ was in His heart.
Along with the day of vengeance, He says the year of His redemption was still far off.

cards.text: Then He says, "I looked," and you can feel the whole scene go quiet. He's looking around for help.

cards.question: When the One from Edom looked for someone to help, what did He find?
How does He say He felt when no one assisted Him?
With no one to help, He says His own ___ brought Him salvation.

cards.text: And He adds, "My own wrath upheld Me." Meanwhile I can't seal ONE cookie box without a baker, which is exactly why you got an invitation, friend.

cards.question: He says the ones He trampled in His anger were the nations.

cards.text: He finishes: "in My wrath I made them drunk and poured out their blood on the ground." No one helped Him, and the One mighty to save did it all with His own arm.

findings.problem: Stop 1, card 3 quotes "It is I, proclaiming vindication.", which isn't the exact BSB wording.

rule.text: Quotes: Quotation marks around Bible words mean the exact BSB wording, punctuation included.

findings.problem: Stop 1, card 8 quotes "I trampled them in My anger and trod them down in My fury.", which isn't the exact BSB wording.

rule.text: Quotes: Quotation marks around Bible words mean the exact BSB wording, punctuation included.

findings.problem: The card puts Isaiah 62:11's "See, your Savior comes!" right before "Now Someone appears," which suggests the One from Edom is that Savior. Isaiah 63:1 does not say who He is. The text leaves that connection open.

rule.text: When he connects two passages, or explains what a law was for, he says only what the texts state.

findings.problem: Genesis 36:1 says "Esau (that is, Edom)." It does not say Edom is the people descended from Esau. Genesis 36:9 ("Esau, the father of the Edomites") supports that fact.

rule.text: Every Bible fact he states carries its reference.

findings.problem: "The question everybody's thinking" adds a crowd. In the text, one unnamed voice asks the question.

rule.text: Leave open what the text leaves open: who is being spoken to, why, or how two things connect.

findings.problem: "Mighty to do what?" asks the baker to finish the wording of the line ("mighty to save"). It does not test the movement or the meaning of the passage.

rule.text: Never ask the baker to guess the next words of a line.

findings.problem: The card spends words defining winepress ("the place where grapes got stomped underfoot"). That belongs in the dictionary pop-up.

rule.text: Don't spend card words explaining a hard word. Hard words get a dictionary pop-up (definitions.md, made after the cards).

findings.problem: "As He tramples them down" uses "them" to point back to card 8, which is no longer on screen. The question doesn't say who "them" is.

rule.text: Always give context in the question. The story card before it isn't on screen anymore, so the question says who and what. Never "him," "that" or "it" pointing back to a card the baker can't see.

findings.problem: Multiple choice dominates the stop: 6 of the 11 choice cards are multiple choice, against 3 fill in the blank and 2 true or false.

rule.text: No stop repeats another stop's pattern, and no type dominates a stop by a wide margin.
